tables.name: Summary
headers: WFX menu comparison: Excel menu vs HTML menu (module by module)
identifiers: WFX menu comparison: Excel menu vs HTML menu (module by module)
rows: Excel file: Menus_2_colored_Admin_corrected.xlsx | HTML file: Menu_Preview_-_Team_Share.html | Excel has 635 menu items in 11 modules; HTML has 252 menu items in 13 modules.
New / List / Search of a shown menu

1. Of 635 Excel menu items, 151 (24%) are available in HTML (same name or renamed/moved), 164 (26%) are sub-menus that HTML does not list under their parent, 120 (19%) are New / List / Search screens that normally sit inside a menu that is in HTML, 160 (25%) are not in HTML, and 38 need confirmation.

2. Finance is the biggest gap. 7 whole sections have no HTML menu (58 Excel items): General Ledger, Inter Company, Taxation & Compliances, Inventory Financials, Fixed Assets, Migrations, GST Doc Integration. HTML shows AP and AR as single entries, so 106 AP, AR and Master sub-menus are not shown (plus their New/List screens).

3. Setup masters are the next gap. Example: of 25 Sales Codes in Excel only 2 are available in HTML Sales Setups. Catalog Codes (UOM, POM, Body Type, Gender, Print Type, Embroidery Type) and Sourcing Codes (Forwarder, Advance Terms, Procurement Type) are also not in HTML.

4. Transaction screens not found in HTML: Process Definition, Good Transfer Note, Alteration / Additional Process, Liability Management, Chargebacks, Supplier Block Booking, Advance License, Sample Value Confirmation, Return-to-Processor and Return-to-Supplier dispatch, OC to OC Roll Transfer, Update Pallet Location.

5. Admin screens not found in HTML: License Info, Batch Jobs, Product Group - Sub Category, Transaction Uniqueness, Internal Settings, Factory Master, and the Inventory, Invoice/ASN, QR Code/Barcode, Stationery and Transaction Sequence configuration rules.

6. HTML adds 86 menus that are not in the Excel (for example Supplier Onboarding, Audits, Recipes, Batch Traceability, Security & Access, Workflow & Approvals, Demand Planning). They are listed at the bottom of each module sheet.
7. The Excel itself has errors to correct (typos, names split across rows, wrong indentation, two rows that are not menus): see sheet Excel Data Errors.
How to read the module sheets
The menu exists in HTML. The Remark says whether it has the same name, was renamed, or moved to another place. "(assumed match)" means I matched it by meaning, so please confirm.
The parent menu is in HTML, but this actual sub-menu is not listed under it (HTML often shows only the parent).
New / List / Search of a shown menu
Excel lists New, List or Search as separate menus. In HTML these are normally tabs or buttons inside the parent menu, so they are not counted as missing.
No menu for this item was found anywhere in the HTML.
There may be a match in HTML but I cannot be sure. Listed in sheet To Confirm with a column for your decision.
The Excel row is not a real menu item (a person name or a requirement note).
Menu exists in HTML but not in the Excel. Shown at the bottom of each module sheet.

Every menu, sub-menu and level in the Excel was compared with every node in the HTML menu data. Items were matched by meaning because the HTML has renamed and re-organised many menus (for example Buyer to Customer, Production to Manufacturing, QC to Quality).
Matches marked "assumed" and everything in To Confirm need a product-owner decision before this report is final.

HTML shows some menus (Finance AP, AR, LC, Setups; Quality Setups; TNA) as single entries without sub-menus. If these sub-menus exist in the real product but are hidden in the preview, they would move from "Sub-menu not shown" to "Available".
